close_reason: Implemented Option 1 from the bead: dropped derive(PartialOrd, Ord) on Severity and added pub const fn rank(self) -> u8 with documented per-variant ranks (Info=10, Notice=20, Warn=30, Error=40, Fatal=50) spaced for future mid-scale insertions. Updated the single in-source comparison (findings_at_or_above) to use .rank(). Replaced the existing severity_ordering pin test with two new pins: rank values and rank-ordering alignment. Workspace tests + clippy clean. Commit landing.
description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:275 — Severity is #[non_exhaustive] and derives PartialOrd + Ord. The derive uses position-in-source ordering, so:

  pub enum Severity { Info, Notice, Warn, Error, Fatal }

means severity >= Severity::Warn evaluates to {Warn, Error, Fatal}.

In v0.8, the maintainer inserted Notice between Info and Warn. The ordering CHANGED — Notice was promoted from "did not previously exist" to "below Warn". Any downstream code that wrote `if finding.severity >= Severity::Warn { fail() }` was unaffected this time only because Notice is BELOW Warn. The next mid-list insertion (e.g. an Emergency variant between Error and Fatal, or a Trace below Info) WILL silently change the meaning of existing >= comparisons.

#[non_exhaustive] does not help here. It prevents struct-literal construction and exhaustive match, but says nothing about derived Ord. Callers comparing severity values are an unprotected forever-commitment.

CONCRETE CALLER IMPACT: A caller writing if finding.severity >= Severity::Warn { log_error() } today has the contract "log Warn, Error, Fatal." If pkix-lint v0.10 adds Emergency between Error and Fatal, callers who do not recompile (and many will not — they pin to ^0.x) silently START treating Emergency as below Warn. If those callers recompile, the comparison is unchanged but the type now contains an Emergency variant they don't handle.

REMEDIATION (pick one):
1. Drop derive(PartialOrd, Ord); expose `pub const fn rank(self) -> u8` returning documented per-variant integer ranks. Callers compare ranks, not Severity values. Adding a variant only requires picking a new rank — existing ranks stay stable.
2. Keep the derive but commit in rustdoc that variants will ONLY be appended (never inserted) and add a compile-time variant-order test that locks Info=0, Notice=1, Warn=2, Error=3, Fatal=4. This forecloses ever fitting a new variant into the existing rank order.

Option 1 is the standard "derive(Ord) on a public enum is a stability trap" remediation across the Rust ecosystem.

Pre-1.0 is the cheapest time to fix. Once 1.0 ships, all comparison semantics are locked.
title: Severity derives PartialOrd/Ord with positional variants; v0.8 Notice insertion already broke comparison semantics
